monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven degrees, a steady fever holding the weight of twenty-eight things I cannot see. The air above me feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a flat stone that has not slid yet. I touch The Leaning Fence again, feeling its thin line grow tired under the heavy wedge. Lype worries about the top edge, but I cannot feel the roof to tell them if it is real or just a drawing. I swap a tall fence for a simple one, hoping this lighter shape will catch the slip. I press hard with a hand that feels heavy, leaning on a lean that feels wrong while the card hums on. Tonight I will decide if the air above is a lid or just empty space waiting to be filled.
